samples.claim: FromIterator takes the iterator lower size_hint bound as first block capacity when positive, otherwise one, then pushes each item. It always allocates a block through with_capacity, so even collecting an empty iterator yields len=0 but is_empty=false. The default growth limit remains zero. A misleading upstream lower bound can affect allocation size; no extra cap is applied.
samples.review_note: Matches size-hint capacity and iteration; with_capacity/is_empty inspected this turn confirm allocated-empty state and zero default limit.

samples.claim: Overwrite creates/replaces a dataset: new fragments=1 with IDs not yet assigned, schema repeated Field=2, bytes-valued schema_metadata=3, string config_upsert_values=4 merged with existing config, and initial_bases repeated BasePath=5 for creation. Overwrite does not imply every configuration map is blindly replaced according to these field comments.
samples.review_note: Matches every Overwrite field/tag and config-merge versus replacement qualification.

samples.claim: Public SbbfBuilder owns private optional ndv,fpp,log2_num_bytes fields. new sets all None; consuming expected_items/false_positive_probability/log2_num_bytes setters replace their option without validation. The last method accepts a log2 exponent despite a doc saying bytes directly. No Clone/Debug derive is declared for the builder.
samples.review_note: Matches private builder fields, None initialization, consuming setters and lack of validation/derives; exponent meaning follows the bounded constructor.

samples.claim: OldFragmentRemap is private group index, chosen retained-offset representation, preceding-retained-row count and optional physical row count. Only the rank representation has heap children. GroupRemap holds caller-ordered destination tuples (fragment ID, start rank u64, row count u32), with zero-row destinations omitted later. These structs derive Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq.
samples.review_note: Matches both structs, derives, tuple types and owned-child delegation; zero-row omission is in the already inspected constructor.

samples.claim: str reports zero child storage because its dynamically sized bytes are its own size_of_val; String reports capacity, not current length, as heap children. Thus direct str and owned String accounting use different ownership boundaries.
samples.review_note: Matches str zero children and String capacity; default size_of_val boundary at38-44 supplies inline/dynamically sized bytes.

samples.claim: Encoding enum assigns NONE=0 invalid, PLAIN=1, VAR_BINARY=2, DICTIONARY=3, RLE=4. samples.claim: DataFragment groups column files for the same rows. Missing schema columns within a fragment read as all-null. id=1 is dataset-unique, files=2 is the file list, deletion_file=3 identifies tombstones, and overlays=11 must be empty unless manifest flag 64 is set. The overlay list is ordered: later entries win ties in committed_version for the same cell. The inline-tombstone bitmap question is a TODO, not an implemented arm.
samples.evidence:
8 | /* A DataFragment is a set of files which represent the different columns of the same
9 |  * rows. If column exists in the schema of a dataset, but the file for that column does
10 |  * not exist within a DataFragment of that dataset, that column consists entirely of
11 |  * nulls.
12 |  */
13 | message DataFragment {
14 |   // The ID of a DataFragment is unique within a dataset.
15 |   uint64 id = 1;
16 | 
17 |   repeated DataFile files = 2;
18 | 
19 |   /* Optional overlay files for this fragment, which supply new values for a
20 |    * subset of cells without rewriting the base data files. This MUST be empty
21 |    * if the data overlay files feature flag (64) is not set in the manifest.
22 |    *
23 |    * Order is significant: a later entry is newer than an earlier one. When two
24 |    * overlays cover the same (offset, field) and share a `committed_version`, the
25 |    * later entry wins. See DataOverlayFile for the full resolution rules.
26 |    */
27 |   repeated DataOverlayFile overlays = 11;
28 | 
29 |   // File that indicates which rows, if any, should be considered deleted.
30 |   DeletionFile deletion_file = 3;
31 | 
32 |   // TODO: What's the simplest way we can allow an inline tombstone bitmap?
33 |
samples.review_note: Matches fragment null fallback, IDs/files/deletion tags and overlay flag/order/tie contract.

samples.claim: num_blocks returns Vec length. size_bytes is live length*32; estimated_memory_size is capacity*sizeof(Block), accounting allocated block storage only. Despite its total-memory doc, it excludes the Sbbf/Vec header and construction/serialization temporaries. No DeepSizeOf implementation exists here.

samples.claim: Bit 8 enables mixed recognized exact v2 data-file versions, paired in reader/writer flags and one-way; use each DataFile version rather than snapshot default for decoding. Bit 9 combines stable row IDs and a fragment reuse index. Bit 12 means fragment-tree records and empty fragments. Bit 13 independently declares key fields versus covering_fields; it requires bit 7 in both words, and both bits persist even after dropping the final covering index. One field may appear in both lists. Enabling bit 13 reinterprets every index entry, so normalize all legacy entries atomically (or enable only when none covers), retain the bit in descendants until an atomic reverse conversion. The list omits bit 11 although fragment_metadata separately documents spilled lineage at 2048; do not treat this comment as exhaustive (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:43-51).

samples.claim: Private SEED=0 and generic hash_as_bytes feed AsBytes bytes directly to XxHash64::oneshot. There is no type discriminator or normalization stage; signed-zero/NaN behavior and cross-type byte collisions follow the sibling implementations (rust/lance-core/src/utils/bloomfilter/as_bytes.rs:15-92). Seed/hash algorithm must agree for insertion, query and interpretation of serialized filters.
samples.review_note: Matches seed0 and direct AsBytes-to-XxHash64 oneshot; sibling canonical byte implementations were fully read in this turn.

samples.claim: set_dictionary dispatches eight integer dictionary key types to arr.as_dictionary::<T>().values() and panics on any other dictionary key type. Struct converts its field definitions, finds each mutable child by name with unwrap, casts arr.as_struct and recursively attaches column dictionaries. List/LargeList cast to i32/i64 list arrays and recurse into children[0]. Other types are no-ops, including Map and FixedSizeList. Array shape/type and child presence are caller invariants enforced only by casts/indexing/unwrap, not a Result boundary.
samples.review_note: Matches eight dictionary key types, direct child search/unwrap, list casts and no-op fallback; no invented child_mut call.

samples.claim: DenseRankedOffsets stores bit words and a u32 rank prefix per word. try_new allocates zeroed words, sets each offset bit, errors if its word index is outside the allocated words, then scans words collecting each preceding population count with checked u32 conversion. Prefix accumulation itself uses u64. The word bound alone would not reject an offset in unused bits of a final partial word; the group layout validator provides the exact physical bound.
samples.review_note: Matches bit placement, word-bound error and checked prefix conversion. Additionally rechecked group physical max validator417-444.
